sentenceSets.sentence: The taciturn expert communicated more through what she declined to confirm than through what she said.

answerChoices.reasoning: Verbose means using many words or overly wordy; the sentence describes someone who communicated through what she declined to say, opposite of using many words.
Loquacious means very talkative; the sentence shows the expert communicating more through silence and refusals than speech.
Garrulous means excessively talkative; the sentence emphasizes communication through decline to confirm, not excessive talking.
Forthcoming means willing to volunteer information; the sentence shows an expert who declines to confirm and withholds words.
Communicative means willing to share information but does not specify reticence; the sentence emphasizes an expert who shared minimally.
Open means willing to share; the sentence describes someone who declined to confirm and was sparing with words.
Sociable means enjoying company and conversation but does not specifically describe reluctance to speak.
Candid means frank and honest but does not require talkativeness; the sentence shows minimalism in speech.
Eloquent means expressive and persuasive in speech; the sentence shows someone who communicated through silence and refusal.
Animated means lively and energetic; the sentence shows an expert who declined to confirm and was sparing with words.
Effusive means expressing emotion in an enthusiastic way; the sentence describes someone who communicated through restraint and silence.

sentenceSets.sentence: Her taciturn nature made interviews difficult; reporters struggled to extract more than monosyllabic responses from her.

answerChoices.reasoning: Talkative means inclined to talk; the sentence describes someone who gave only monosyllabic responses, opposite of talkative.
Chatty means friendly and inclined to conversation; the sentence shows difficulty extracting responses, opposite of chatty nature.
Expansive means inclined to elaborate or express freely; the sentence shows limited monosyllabic responses only.
Voluble means disposed to talk readily; the sentence shows a nature that made reporters struggle to get responses.
Accessible means easy to talk to or reach but the sentence emphasizes difficulty extracting responses.
Transparent means open and not hiding things but does not address willingness to talk; the sentence emphasizes verbal reticence.
Extroverted means outgoing but does not specifically describe reluctance to speak.
Effusive means expressing emotions enthusiastically but does not necessarily describe talkativeness; the sentence shows minimal responses.
Mysterious means puzzling or enigmatic but does not directly describe reluctance to speak; the sentence emphasizes minimal verbal responses.
Aloof means distant emotionally but does not specifically describe speech patterns; the sentence emphasizes verbal reticence.
Evasive means avoiding commitment but implies deliberate dodging; the sentence shows minimal responses rather than strategic avoidance.

sentenceSets.sentence: The taciturn coach rarely praised his players explicitly, instead showing approval only through subtle gestures and increased playing time.

answerChoices.reasoning: Expressive means readily showing feelings through words or gestures; the sentence shows approval shown through subtle gestures, not explicit expression.
Demonstrative means openly displaying emotions and feelings; the sentence shows approval that was subtle and rarely explicit.
Vocal means expressed through speech; the sentence shows a coach who rarely praised explicitly, communicating through other means.
Effusive means expressing emotions enthusiastically; the sentence shows approval shown through subtle means, not enthusiastic speech.
Talkative means inclined to talk but does not specifically describe showing approval; the sentence emphasizes a coach who rarely praised verbally.
Outspoken means frank and candid in speech but the sentence emphasizes subtle communication rather than candid praise.
Encouraging means giving confidence but does not require explicit verbal praise; the sentence shows approval through subtle means.
Amiable means pleasant and friendly but does not directly describe verbal patterns or willingness to praise.
Harsh means severe or unpleasant; the sentence shows a coach who showed approval through increased playing time, indicating support.
Critical means inclined to criticize but the sentence shows a coach who showed approval through subtle means.
Dismissive means showing no concern; the sentence shows a coach who demonstrated approval through playing time and gestures.
